title: Shut the back door
briefing: A security scan flags app-01: the ancient 'telnet' service is running.
telnet sends passwords in clear text across the network. It should never
run on a production box — and right now it's active AND enabled at boot.
tips: `systemctl list-units` shows everything running. Look for telnet.
Two fixes are needed: stop it now, and disable it so it never comes back.
objective: Shut down the insecure telnet service and stop it from ever starting again — it must end up inactive and disabled.
expert_objective: Remove the telnet attack surface from app-01, now and at boot.
hints: Confirm it's up: `systemctl status telnet` (active, enabled).
Stop it now: `sudo systemctl stop telnet`. Then keep it off at boot: `sudo systemctl disable telnet`.
One line does both: `sudo systemctl disable --now telnet`.
solution:
systemctl status telnet
sudo systemctl stop telnet
sudo systemctl disable telnet
explanation: Hardening a box means removing what shouldn't run. `stop` ends the process now; `disable` stops it starting at the next boot. You need both — a service you only stopped will quietly return after a reboot. `disable --now` does the pair in one go.
